Senses.Explanation: An interrogative pronoun: 'who?' or, according to syntax, 'whom?' The records put it to several public uses. It asks a monk's identity inside the exchange 'what is buddha?' — 'who are you?' / 'so-and-so' / 'do you recognize so-and-so?' (汝是阿誰／某甲／汝識某甲否). It asks lineage in the stock interview formula 'whose song does the master sing; to whom does the house style succeed?' (師唱誰家曲，宗風嗣阿誰), agency in 'who can go?' (阿誰去得), authorship in 'who spoke this scripture?' (此經是阿誰說), and the beneficiary of activity in 'for whom are you busy every day?' (每日區區為阿誰). The Chan deviation lies in this concentration inside public identity, lineage, authorship, and accountability questions; the word itself remains the ordinary interrogative and does not name a special inward self.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 2,924 hits in 345 texts. Family comparison: 'who?' (誰) and 'which one?' (阿那箇) are interrogatives; 'that one' (那箇) and 'this one' (這箇) are demonstratives; 'who?' (阿誰) does not acquire a separate 'true self' sense merely because identity is sometimes its subject. Agent, author, beneficiary, and lineage predecessor are different answers to the same pronoun, not different referents encoded by the word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是佛。師曰。汝是阿誰。曰。某甲。師曰。汝識某甲否。曰。分明箇。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Public identity questioning follows 'what is buddha?': who are you, and do you recognize the conventional self-name supplied?

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：師唱誰家曲，宗風嗣阿誰？師云：窣堵那叱掌上擎。僧曰：恁麼則北塔嫡子，韶石兒孫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Stock lineage interview asking whose house style the master succeeds to; the follow-up names lineage descent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。此經是阿誰說。僧抗聲曰。禪師相弄。豈不知是佛說耶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Authorship question: 'who spoke this scripture?' The lecturer answers that Buddha did.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師謂眾曰。我要一人。傳語西堂。阿誰去得。五峯曰。某甲去。師曰。汝作麼生傳語。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Agency question to the assembly: who can carry a message to Xitang? Wufeng volunteers and is questioned further.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲巖問和尚每日區區為阿誰師曰有一人要巖曰囙甚麼不教伊自作師曰他無家活
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunyan asks for whom the master is busy every day; the exchange supplies 'there is one who needs it.'

Senses.Explanation: Ananda is deployed in the Chan record as the figure who questions the succession after the Buddha. He asks Kashyapa, “besides the gold-thread robe transmitted by the World-Honored One, what else was transmitted?” Kashyapa calls his name; Ananda answers; Kashyapa says, “knock down the flagpole before the gate.” Later masters raise the exchange as a public case and add their own comments: one says that before the flagpole is down it pierces people's skulls and changes their eyes, then asks where old man Shakyamuni is seen after it falls. The robe question and flagpole response, rather than a general life story, are Ananda's primary Chan deployment. The records also place him in direct exchanges with the Buddha. In one repeatedly raised bowl case, the Buddha tells him to enter the city carrying the bowl; when Ananda asks for the procedure of the seven buddhas, the Buddha calls “Ananda,” Ananda answers, and the Buddha says, “carry the bowl and go.” At another seated assembly Ananda strikes the sounding block and asks the World-Honored One to speak the teaching. The transmission record later says that Ananda finished entrusting the eye-treasury of the teaching. Thus the name repeatedly occupies public questioning, assembly, and succession positions in cases later masters cite.
Senses.Note: Across the cited Chan records, Ananda recurs as the questioner in the robe-and-flagpole succession exchange and as the respondent to a direct name-call. The entry is limited to those recorded exchanges, teaching-seat actions, and transmission notices.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日問迦葉曰。師兄。世尊傳金襴袈裟外。別傳箇甚麼。迦葉召阿難。阿難應諾。迦葉曰。倒却門前剎竿著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The succession case records Ananda's robe question, Kashyapa's name-call, Ananda's answer, and the instruction to knock down the gate-front flagpole.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉阿難問迦葉：世尊傳金襴外，別傳何法？迦葉召阿難，阿難應諾。迦葉曰：倒却門前剎竿著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later master publicly raises the same robe-and-flagpole exchange as a case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 迦葉曰：倒却門前剎竿著。師曰：剎竿未倒，穿却諸人髑髏，換却諸人眼睛。剎竿倒後，向甚麼處見釋迦老子？參！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The later comment distinguishes the flagpole before and after its fall and asks where old man Shakyamuni is then seen.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉世尊一日勅阿難食時將至汝當入城持鉢阿難應諾世尊曰汝既持鉢須依過去七佛議式阿難便問如何是七佛儀式世尊召阿難阿難應諾世尊曰持鉢去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later address raises the bowl case: Ananda asks about the procedure, answers when called, and is told to carry the bowl and go.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊一日陞座。默然而坐。阿難白椎曰。請世尊說法。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: At the teaching seat, Ananda strikes the sounding block and asks the World-Honored One to speak the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 本來付有法付了言無法各各須自悟悟了無無法阿難付法眼藏竟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A lamp narrative closes its transmission verse by saying that Ananda finished entrusting the eye-treasury of the teaching.
